questions.prompt: Which API test strategy gives the most confidence?
options: Use a production database so test data matches customer data.
Treat code coverage alone as proof of correct API semantics.
Cover success and negative paths, schemas, authentication/authorization boundaries, repeatability, and contract behavior.
Test only the root page in a browser and assume every route works.
questions.answer_key: Cover success and negative paths, schemas, authentication/authorization boundaries, repeatability, and contract behavior.
questions.explanation: Cover success and negative paths, schemas, authentication/authorization boundaries, repeatability, and contract behavior. This is especially relevant to “Unit Testing” because the API contract must remain explicit and reviewable.

questions.prompt: For the lesson “Unit Testing”, which check provides the strongest practical evidence?
options: Test against production records so the exercise cannot be repeated safely.
Run deterministic success, negative, auth, schema, and contract tests in an isolated environment.
Rely on a code review comment without running any representative check.
Run one happy-path call and skip invalid, denied, and failure scenarios.
questions.answer_key: Run deterministic success, negative, auth, schema, and contract tests in an isolated environment.
questions.explanation: A useful check is repeatable, tied to an observable contract, and includes an important negative or boundary scenario.

questions.prompt: Which review warning is most relevant to “Unit Testing”?
options: The suite ignores authorization boundaries, failure paths, or repeatability.
The expected behavior and relevant failure cases are documented.
A representative test can reproduce the result.
The API avoids exposing internal secrets and personal data.
questions.answer_key: The suite ignores authorization boundaries, failure paths, or repeatability.
questions.explanation: This finding weakens a core API guarantee and should be treated as a design or release issue, not only a style concern.
